title: Amazon Prime Big Deal Days (fall Prime event, 48 hours, Oct 6-7) — the nonstore distortion this calendar tracks only in summer
source: EST: aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-prime-big-deals-day-2026-when-october-6-7 states verbatim '48 hours of Prime member-exclusive deals across more than 35 categories' starting 'October 6', with deal drops at 'midnight, 8 a.m., and 1 p.m. PDT' across 'Prime members in 22 countries including ... the United States'; secondary reads (nbcnews.com, today.com, 9to5toys.com, gsmarena.com, all dated 2026-09-15) put the window at 12:01 a.m. PT Tue Oct 6 to 11:59 p.m. Wed Oct 7. Fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200) — Amazon's own newsroom, which for a tracked issuer would ordinarily carry an `IR:` prefix. Filed estimate on two counts, neither of them date doubt: this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and only one primary page was read this session against the two the advance-services-q3-2026-11-19 precedent requires before promotion (the same bar retail-ecommerce-q3-2026-11-19 and costco-q4-fy2026-2026-09-24 were held to). Day 1 of the two-day window per house convention. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: The load-bearing distortion in this calendar's retail complex is an Amazon scheduling decision, and Amazon's schedule has never been on the calendar. retail-sales-2026-09-16 has rested every row since 2026-08-19 on one mechanism: Amazon moved the SUMMER Prime Day from July to June in 2026, which pulled nonstore spend forward, printed nonstore -2.2% in July, and created the +0.41pp headline / +0.76pp control-group unwind that is two thirds of that ledger's mechanical base case (FT-retail-sales-2026-09-16-3 tests it directly). Four Census retail prints are tracked and the quarterly e-commerce report was added on 2026-09-09, but the event that MOVES the series was invisible. This entry fixes that, and it carries a finding of its own: the FALL event does not distort. Prime Big Deal Days ran 2025-10-07/08 (aboutamazon.com's own 2025 post, read 2026-09-15) and runs 2026-10-06/07 — both squarely inside October in both years, one day apart, so unlike the summer event there is no cross-month base effect for the October reference period. The consequence for this calendar is that retail-sales-2026-11-17 (October data) inherits a CLEAN nonstore comparison, and the Prime artefact that has dominated the 09-16 ledger for 28 days is a summer-only phenomenon rather than a standing feature of the series. Filed low impact and kind `sector` deliberately: it is a promotional window rather than a scheduled disclosure, no house playbook is keyed to it, and AMZN is a tracked NAME here only through the rate/duration channel plus its direct nonstore exposure - it is NOT in src/domain/earnings-calendar.ts and this proposal does not add it. CONSIDERED AND DECLINED alongside it, so their absence reads as a decision: Amazon's own Q3 earnings date was not announced on any primary read this session and is not filed on a pattern; NRF's holiday-sales forecast has no pinned 2026 date; Redbook is a standing weekly with no discrete date; and the Census retail complex (retail-sales 09-16/10-15/11-17/12-16, retail-ecommerce-q3-2026-11-19, retail-benchmark-revision-2026-09-28, census-benchmark-revision-nsa-2026-09-28, mtis) is already tracked end to end. Discovered during the retail-sales-2026-09-16 D-1 pulse (2026-09-15), on the day Amazon announced it.
